what_its_for: Deucravacitinib is used to treat moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis in adults. Psoriasis is a skin condition that causes red, scaly, itchy patches on your skin. This medicine helps calm the part of your immune system that causes these skin flare-ups.
how_to_take: Swallow the tablet whole with or without food. Do not crush, split, or chew the tablet. Try to take it at the same time every day to help you remember. Wash your hands before and after handling the tablet.
dosing: The usual dose is one 6 mg tablet taken by mouth once every day. Always take the dose your doctor prescribed. Do not take more or less than directed without talking to your doctor first.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember on the same day. If you do not remember until the next day, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at the regular time. Never take two doses in one day to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store deucravacitinib at room temperature between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep it in the original container with the lid tightly closed. Keep it away from moisture, heat, and direct sunlight. Store it in a safe place out of reach of children and pets. Do not use after the expiration date printed on the package.
what_to_avoid: Avoid receiving live vaccines (such as the chickenpox or MMR vaccine) while taking this medicine, as it may make them less safe or effective. Talk to your doctor before getting any vaccines. Avoid being around people who are sick with infections when possible. Limit your time in the sun and use sunscreen, as psoriasis medicines may slightly increase your skin cancer risk over time. Do not stop taking the medicine without talking to your doctor first.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away if you notice any of the following: signs of infection such as fever, chills, cough, painful urination, or wounds that do not heal; unusual skin changes or new growths on your skin; cold sores or shingles (painful blistering rash); symptoms of low blood cell counts such as unusual tiredness, pale skin, or frequent infections; chest pain, shortness of breath, or leg swelling; or any new or worsening symptoms that concern you. Also tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding.
when_it_works: Most people start to see some improvement in their skin within 4 to 16 weeks of starting treatment. It may take up to 6 months to see the full benefits of the medicine. Everyone responds differently, so be patient and keep taking the medicine as directed even if you do not notice changes right away.
special_populations: Pregnancy and breastfeeding: It is not known if this medicine is safe during pregnancy or breastfeeding. Talk to your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding before starting this medicine. Older adults: This medicine can generally be used in older adults, but your doctor will monitor you closely for any side effects. Kidney or liver problems: Tell your doctor if you have kidney or liver disease, as your dose or monitoring may need to be adjusted. Children: This medicine is currently only approved for adults and should not be used in children.
